slides.title: PowerPoint Templates & Themes 🎨
slides.text: A PowerPoint template is a pre-designed slide layout with placeholders for text and images. A theme is a coordinated set of colors, fonts, and effects applied across all slides for a professional look!
slides.spoken: A PowerPoint template is a pre-designed slide layout with placeholders for text and images. A theme is a coordinated set of colors, fonts, and effects applied across all slides!

slides.title: Charts & Slide Sorter View 📊
slides.text: You can insert charts like bar charts and pie charts to display numbers visually. Slide Sorter view shows all your slide thumbnails at once, making it super easy to rearrange or delete slides!
slides.spoken: You can insert charts like bar charts and pie charts to display numbers visually. Slide Sorter view shows all your slide thumbnails at once so you can rearrange them easily!

slides.title: From Algorithm to Code 🤖
slides.text: An algorithm is your human-friendly, step-by-step plan to solve a problem—like a recipe! When you write that plan in a programming language like Scratch, it becomes a program the computer runs.
slides.spoken: An algorithm is your step-by-step plan to solve a problem, like a recipe. When written in a programming language like Scratch, it becomes a program!

slides.title: The Scratch Interface 🎪
slides.text: Scratch is a visual programming language! The Stage is where your sprite performs, the Blocks palette holds color-coded command blocks, and the Scripts area is where you snap blocks together like LEGO bricks.
slides.spoken: Scratch is a visual programming language. The Stage is where your sprite performs, the Blocks palette holds command blocks, and the Scripts area is where you snap them together!

slides.title: Sprites & Scratch Scripts ⚡
slides.text: Sprites are characters that act on the stage. You can draw them in the Paint Editor and save them! Scripts start with Event hat blocks (like green flag clicked) followed by motion, looks, and sound blocks.
slides.spoken: Sprites are characters that act on the stage. You can draw them in the Paint Editor and save them. Scripts start with Event hat blocks followed by motion, looks, and sound blocks!

challenges.answer: A pre-designed slide layout with placeholders for text and images

challenges.question: What is the difference between an algorithm and a program?
challenges.answer: An algorithm is a human-friendly plan; a program is that plan written in code
options: An algorithm is a human-friendly plan; a program is that plan written in code
An algorithm and a program are exactly the same thing
An algorithm is computer code; a program is a paper drawing
challenges.hint: Think of an algorithm as a recipe and a program as the instructions followed by a computer!
challenges.misconception: An algorithm is the human-friendly step-by-step plan, while a program is that exact plan written in a programming language for a computer!

challenges.question: Drag each Scratch block to its correct category!
challenges.hint: When green flag clicked = Event! Move 10 steps = Motion! Say Hello = Looks!
challenges.misconception: Remember: Event blocks start scripts, Motion blocks move sprites, Looks blocks change appearance, and Sound blocks play audio!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. When green flag clicked = Event! Move 10 steps = Motion! Say Hello = Looks!

challenges.question: Why must a Scratch script almost always start with an Event block?
challenges.answer: To give the computer a starting signal or trigger when to run
options: To give the computer a starting signal or trigger when to run
To make the sprite change its color automatically
To save the project file to the computer
challenges.hint: Think of a starter whistle in a running race! What starts the script?
challenges.misconception: An event block acts like a starter whistle; without it, the computer has no trigger signal to know when to run the script!
